ai.description: *Hemidactylus siva* is a small gecko reaching 5–6 cm SVL. It is pale brown with dark dorsal crossbands and possesses distinctive, enlarged, strongly keeled tubercles and a slender, unsegmented tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemidactylus siva* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous dark stripe running from the snout through the eye to the neck, lacking in similar species.
ai.habitat: The Hampi Rock Gecko inhabits granite boulder landscapes within dry deciduous forests and rocky outcrops, typically found at elevations between 300 and 600 meters.
ai.behavior: The Hampi Rock Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage on rock surfaces and crevices for small insects and arthropods.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus siva* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs primarily during the monsoon season, from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Hampi Rock Gecko (*Hemidactylus siva*) is endemic to the rocky landscapes of northern Karnataka and neighboring regions in the Deccan Plateau of peninsular India.
